text: The Agusta A.106 was a single-seat light helicopter developed to serve as an anti-submarine warfare (ASW) platform for the Impavido-class destroyers of the Italian Navy. It was equipped with a sophisticated electronics suite supplied by Ferranti, enabling autostabilisation and contact identification. The helicopter could carry two torpedoes beneath its fuselage. Its tail and two-bladed main rotor were designed to fold for storage on ships, and the skid undercarriage included fittings for flotation bags. Two prototypes were constructed, with the first one achieving flight in November 1965. A planned pre-production batch of five aircraft was cancelled by the Italian Navy in 1973. Data for this information is sourced from Jane's All The World's Aircraft 1969-70 [1]. General characteristics, performance, armament, and comparisons with other aircraft of similar role, configuration, and era are also documented.
